title: Token-slice observability and compatibility layer for streamed outputs
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood's streaming API returns incremental output (slices) for low-latency UX. Current telemetry is coarse-grained (request-level) and does not reliably attribute metrics to streamed fragments, function/tool calls, or structured output boundaries. This makes it difficult to: diagnose per-slice latency spikes, correlate tool call failures with the originating token span, and ensure PII-sensitive content in streams is redacted before logs/backends ingest it.

Goal:
Add a token-slice observability model that: (1) emits per-slice metrics (latency, token-count, kv-cache hits, batching attribution), (2) attaches tracing spans that map back to the parent request and to any function/tool call events emitted mid-stream, and (3) enforces log-redaction and a compatibility shim so older SDKs/clients can consume new structured stream events without breaking.

Scope / Non-Goals:
- Includes runtime telemetry hooks, SDK event contract changes, Console ingestion updates, and a compatibility shim for legacy SSE/HTTP clients.
- Does NOT include storage/long-term retention policy changes (separate work).

Success metrics:
- Per-slice latency histograms visible in Console for 95th/99th percentile per minute.
- End-to-end trace linking from request -> slice -> tool call -> tool response in 90% of sampled streams.
- Zero PII leaks in streaming logs for redaction-tested patterns in our sample prompt set.

Engineering constraints/considerations:
- Keep overhead minimal: sampling rate default 1% for high-throughput customers, full sampling for P0 debug cycles.
- Compatibility: introduce new event envelope "slice_event_v2" while supporting legacy "chunk" events via shim in SDK/runtime.
- Security: redaction must run before events hit any non-ephemeral log sinks.

References:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Token+Slice+Observability+Proposal
- Runtime PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8462
- SDK changes PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/411
- Console ingestion design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Stream+Telemetry+Ingestion
acceptance_criteria: Console shows per-slice latency histograms and per-request slice counts for sample workload
Tracing UI can link a request trace to individual slice spans and to tool-call spans for at least 90% sampled flows
SDKs can opt-in to 'slice_event_v2' and legacy clients gracefully fall back to parsed chunk events via compatibility shim
Redaction rules applied to streamed events block known PII patterns from reaching non-ephemeral logs in test harness
Added e2e test that simulates a function/tool call mid-stream and verifies metric and span correlation
steps: Design: finalize slice event schema and span correlation keys (slice_id, parent_request_id, tool_call_id)
Runtime: add lightweight slice instrumentation points, emit metrics and open/close trace spans around each slice emission
Runtime: integrate pre-log redaction pipeline for streamed payloads using token-aware regex + heuristic filters
SDK: implement compatibility shim that maps slice_event_v2 to legacy chunk frames for older clients
Console: update ingestion pipeline and dashboards to accept slice-level metrics and trace links
QA: create synthetic prompt set with structured outputs and tool calls, verify metrics, spans, and redaction
Rollout: feature-flag rollout, watch sampling signals and error budget impact; progressively increase sample rate for debug customers
